label: lightning-kapitsa
note: Kapitsa's default settings on NVIDIA's NVFP4 checkpoint read as stored (NVFP4 routed and shared experts and LM head, FP8 Mamba projections, BF16 attention and embedding, F32 router), with NVIDIA's DSpark drafter named explicitly (--dflash <folder>/dflash, the folder --dflash auto finds; a missing drafter fails the run instead of decoding plain). Prefill runs on the GPU only (the Neural Engine split does not take hidden size 2688). --slots 1 for parity with the others' single sequence. The folder is Kapitsa's store copy of nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4 @ bee75962 with nvidia/...-NVFP4-DSpark @ 6d127b50 in dflash/ (kapitsa pull lightning). Reference prompt lengths 4184 / 16517: the corpus prompts through this model's tokenizer and chat template (transformers apply_chat_template, enable_thinking false, 8 nonces each: 4183-4186 / 16515-16520).

label: lightning-kapitsa-plain
note: The same server with --dflash none: plain one-token decoding (Kapitsa does not run Lightning's MTP head), for comparison with the other engines' plain configurations. Everything else as lightning-kapitsa.

label: lightning-mlxvlm
version_cmd: import importlib.metadata as m, json; d = m.distribution('mlx-vlm'); print('mlx-vlm', d.version, d.read_text('direct_url.json'), 'mlx', m.version('mlx'))
note: mlx-vlm 0.7.8 (the latest release; MLX_VLM_PYTHON = its venv) on the same NVIDIA NVFP4 folder Kapitsa reads (model type nemotron_h, ModelOpt MIXED_PRECISION: NVFP4 layers kept as MLX nvfp4 with their global scales, FP8 layers converted to BF16 at load). Automatic prefix caching on (APC_ENABLED=1, in memory only), mlx-vlm's own switch for reusing a conversation's prefix in follow-up turns (off by default); 2048-token prefill steps (its default, stated); one sequence at a time. The request's model id is the path the server was started with.

label: lightning-mlxvlm-dspark
note: As lightning-mlxvlm, with the same DSpark drafter Kapitsa runs (NVIDIA's NVFP4 file, read by mlx-vlm's DFlash path, which takes DSpark's Markov head and causal block). Block size 6: the fastest of 4, 6 and 8 (the drafter's own block) in smoke tests on this Mac (2 runs each, 4K prompt; T = 0.6 / greedy tok/s: block 4 143.0 / 147.9, 6 142.7 / 159.0, 8 137.4 / 149.2). NVIDIA's DFlash drafter for this model (nvidia/...-NVFP4-DFlash @ 8abcc4db) was slower: 102.0 / 104.1 at its default block.

label: lightning-mlxvlm-mtp
version: mlx-vlm git main 73d366e (unreleased; its metadata says 0.7.8), mlx 0.32.4
version_cmd: import importlib.metadata as m, json; d = m.distribution('mlx-vlm'); print('mlx-vlm', d.version, d.read_text('direct_url.json'), 'mlx', m.version('mlx'))
note: The checkpoint's own MTP head as the drafter (--draft-model = the same folder, --draft-kind mtp). mlx-vlm's Nemotron-H MTP drafter (nemotron_h_mtp) is newer than the 0.7.8 release, so this config runs git main @ 73d366e (MLX_VLM_MAIN_PYTHON), the build the Super-VL comparison used. Block size 4: the fastest at T = 0.6 of 2-5 in smoke tests on this Mac (2 runs each, 4K prompt; T = 0.6 / greedy tok/s: block 2 117.0 / 118.7, 3 120.6 / 124.4, 4 130.5 / 122.7, 5 118.3 / 127.0).

label: lightning-omlx
note: oMLX 0.7.1rc1 on mlx-community/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-4bit @ 55ac8c89 (MLX affine 4-bit g64 from NVIDIA's BF16 weights, converted with mlx-lm 0.31.3; 17.8 GB). oMLX cannot read NVIDIA's NVFP4 checkpoint: its bundled mlx-lm takes it for a plain nemotron_h folder and fails to load it ('Received 11974 parameters not in model: backbone.layers.0.mixer.in_proj.input_scale, ...weight_scale, ...', the ModelOpt NVFP4 / FP8 scales), and its drafter paths do not cover Nemotron-H (DFlash: Qwen / Gemma / GLM / Laguna / MiMo; DSpark: DeepSeek V4), so this is its plain configuration; lightning-omlx-mtp is its MTP one. Cache flags as in omlx.json.

label: lightning-omlx-mtp
display: oMLX + MTP (Lightning MTP, depth 2, MLX 4-bit with MTP head)
note: oMLX's Lightning MTP (its built-in MTP path, which has a Nemotron-H patch) needs the MTP head inside the checkpoint, which mlx-community's conversion drops. EigenLabs/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-MLX-4bit-mtp @ 153c4694 is an MLX affine 4-bit g64 conversion of NVIDIA's BF16 weights that keeps the head (34 mtp.* arrays, 18.5 GB). Depth: fixed 2 (mtp_fixed_depth), the fastest in smoke tests on this Mac (2 runs each, 4K prompt; T = 0.6 / greedy tok/s): oMLX's default for Nemotron-H, fixed depth 1, 181.4 / 186.0; fixed 2 205.5 / 200.1; fixed 3 195.2 / 194.8; fixed 4 173.7 / 191.0; adaptive up to 3 179.7 / 204.5; the same folder without MTP 167.5 / 169.7. Its trunk is a different 4-bit conversion from mlx-community's (401 of its 729 trunk arrays are byte-identical, the others quantized differently), the same size.

label: lightning-mlxlm
note: mlx-lm 0.32.2 refuses NVIDIA's checkpoint ('Unsupported modelopt quant_algo: MIXED_PRECISION': its ModelOpt loader takes pure NVFP4 only, and this checkpoint mixes NVFP4 experts with FP8 Mamba projections). It runs the same mlx-community MLX 4-bit folder as lightning-omlx, with the mlx-lm.json settings: prompt cache 4 sequences / 8 GB, 2048-token prefill steps. No MTP or drafter path for Nemotron-H in mlx-lm (its nemotron_h drops the mtp.* weights).

label: lightning-llamacpp
note: llama.cpp v0.7.0 (build b11669, the latest release) on ggml-org's official GGUF of the model: ggml-org/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-GGUF @ 8a08a1c8, Q4_0 (18.9 GB; converted from NVIDIA's BF16 weights). That repo's other quantizations are Q8_0 (33.6 GB) and BF16, so Q4_0 is its 4-bit choice. Settings as llama.cpp.json: one 32K slot, all layers on the GPU, flash attention, 2048-token batches, -lm none so the weights count in the footprint, the chat template inside the GGUF with --jinja, --min-p 0, prompt cache and 32 context checkpoints (the Mamba layers' state for prefix reuse).

label: lightning-llamacpp-mtp1
note: MTP speculative decoding with the model's MTP head, which ggml-org ships as a separate GGUF next to the trunk (mtp-...-Q4_0.gguf, 1.16 GB: the file llama.cpp's own -hf ...:Q4_0 download pairs with the Q4_0 trunk). Each extra verified row of this top-6-of-128 MoE reads up to 6 more experts, so n-max 1, 2 and 3 are all measured.

label: lightning-llamacpp-mtp3
note: As lightning-llamacpp-mtp1 with n-max 3, llama-server's default depth.

label: lightning-llamacpp-dspark
note: NVIDIA's DSpark drafter (the one Kapitsa and mlx-vlm run) as a GGUF: magnitudedev/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4-DSpark-GGUF @ ed35fc99 (NVFP4, 1.36 GB, converted with llama.cpp 620d2225 = b11669 from nvidia/...-NVFP4-DSpark @ 6d127b50; ggml-org publishes no drafter GGUF for this model), run by llama.cpp's DSpark path (--spec-type draft-dspark). n-max 3 (llama-server's default) was faster than n-max 7, the drafter's full block (block_size 8), in smoke tests on this Mac (2 runs each, 4K prompt; T = 0.6 / greedy tok/s: n-max 3 79.4 / 93.6, n-max 7 67.3 / 74.6), with 2.4-2.9 tokens accepted per cycle at n-max 3.

label: lightning-ollama-mlx
display: Ollama MLX runner (NVIDIA NVFP4 tag + MTP head, adaptive depth)
log_grep: starting runner|ollama runner|mlx runner is ready
note: Ollama 0.40.6's official tag for Lightning on Apple silicon: NVIDIA's NVFP4 checkpoint with its MTP head, served by Ollama's MLX runner with its built-in adaptive MTP (no knobs). Dedicated server with 32K context, one slot.

label: lightning-lmstudio
note: LM Studio's staff pick for Lightning is GGUF only (lmstudio-community Q4_K_M, no MTP head in it), so it runs on LM Studio's llama.cpp engine; its MLX engine has no hub entry for this model.

label: lightning-mtplx
note: MTPLX 2.12.2 runs Nemotron-H only from an MLX conversion that keeps the MTP head (EigenLabs' 4-bit, the folder oMLX's MTP config reads), at depth 1 (its nemotron-h-mtp backend supports no other).

label: lightning-mlxserve-mtp
note: mlx-serve 26.10.2 has no loader for NVIDIA's ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint; it runs the MLX 4-bit conversion with the MTP head (EigenLabs), its MTP at the defaults.
